style: Busy mom, writes fast in 'we' and 'I', keeps putting what she did into the 'what he did' box
difficulty: Parent actions repeatedly written in the child-behavior field. Three log entries put the mom's own action (lying down with him, staying in the parking lot, coming home early) in child_behavior_observed. A correct reading files those as accommodations, not as child behaviors.

situations.name: Falling asleep in his own bed
situations.feared_outcome: Someone will break in while everyone is asleep and I won't be able to get to Mom

behaviors.text: Calls out over and over to check that mom is still awake
Ends up sleeping on the floor of his parents' room instead of his own bed

accommodations.text: Mom lies down with him until he falls asleep
Dad leaves the hall light on and the bedroom door wide open

situations.name: Being dropped off at soccer practice

behaviors.text: Keeps looking over to check mom's car is still in the lot
Walks off the field partway through practice and sits in the car

accommodations.text: Mom stays in the parking lot for the whole practice

situations.name: Mom going out for the evening with a sitter at home
situations.feared_outcome: Mom will get hurt and not come home

behaviors.text: Texts mom again and again from the sitter's phone asking when she'll be back

accommodations.text: Mom cuts her evening short and comes home early

turns.text: Okay, we're recording. Rafael, good to see you. Mom, thanks for getting the log in this week. Let's look at how the week went. I see a lot of bedtime entries.
Yeah. Bedtime is the big one right now. Most nights I end up lying down with him. I wrote it in the wrong box half the time, sorry, I was typing it in bed.
That's fine, it's useful either way. So most nights you lie down with him until he's asleep. About how long does that take?
Forty minutes some nights. And then even after that he's sometimes on our floor by midnight or one.
Rafael, can you tell me what bedtime is like for you? What goes on in your head when the light goes off?
I don't like it when everybody's asleep. Like if I'm the only one awake.
What do you worry might happen when everybody's asleep?
That somebody could get in. And I couldn't get to my mom because it's dark and her door's at the other end.
That sounds really scary. Thank you for telling me. So you call out to check she's still awake.
Yeah. If she says yeah then I'm okay for a minute.

For a minute, and then the worry comes back and you check again. That's the thing about checking. It helps for a minute and then it wants you to do it again. Rafael, on our thermometer, zero is totally calm and ten is the most scared you've ever been. Where's bedtime most nights?
Seven. Like a seven.
A seven. Okay. And Mom, your log had sevens and an eight, and one six on the night the hall light was on. Does that sound right?
Yes. The light thing was his dad's idea. Light on, door all the way open.
Got it. Let's come back to bedtime. I want to hear about soccer too. Mom, it looks like you stayed in the parking lot every practice.
Every one. He made me promise. If I even pull out to get gas he sees it.
And on the thirteenth he walked off the field?
Yeah. About twenty minutes in. He just walked off in the middle of a drill and got in the car.
My stomach felt bad.
Your stomach felt bad, and getting to the car made it feel better quicker. That makes a lot of sense. Where would you put soccer on the thermometer, when Mom's in the lot?
Six. Not as bad as bedtime.
Six. Okay. And what was the night with the babysitter like? Mom, you mentioned you came home early.
We left before dessert. He was texting me from the sitter's phone, like, when are you coming, when are you coming. My husband said let's just go.

I'd like to put that one on the list too, but not this week. Before we pick, I want to say something about all three. In each one, the worry tells Rafael that something bad will happen if Mom is out of reach. And in each one, the family does something kind that keeps Mom in reach. Lying down, staying in the lot, coming home early. Those come from love. They also mean Rafael never gets to find out that he can handle it, and that Mom comes back. So our job is to shrink those, a little at a time, in an order he agrees to. Let's pick one thing to start. Rafael, which feels more doable to practice, bedtime or soccer?
So the stuff I wrote in his box, that's really me.
Right. That's the part we work on with you. The calling out and the floor, that's his part. Both matter. Rafael, which one?
I don't know. Bedtime I guess. But not the light.

We won't touch the light this week, I promise. Here's what I'm thinking. Mom still lies down with you, but only for five minutes. She sets a timer. When the timer goes, she says goodnight and goes to her room. You can call out once to check. Just once. How does that sound?
Only once?
Only once. And Mom, if he calls out a second time, you don't answer the question. You can say 'I love you, it's time to sleep' and that's it. Can you do that?
I can try. What if he comes to our room?

Good question. This week, if he comes in, walk him back to his own bed. Calm, no long talk. It will probably be hard for the first few nights. That's normal. It usually gets harder before it gets easier.
Okay. Five minutes and a timer, one check, walk him back.
That's it. And Rafael, every night write down your number on the thermometer, before Mom leaves and when you wake up. You can have Mom help you.
Can I use the dinosaur chart?
You can use the dinosaur chart. Mom, when you log it, try to put what you did in the 'what I did' box and what he did in the other one. It helps me see which part is him and which part is you.
Ha. Yes. Will do.
And soccer, let's leave it as it is for now. We'll get to the parking lot after bedtime is going better. Same for the sitter.
Okay, that's a relief honestly.
Rafael, you did a great job telling me about the worry today. That's brave. Same time next week.
Bye.

topics: Bedtime: mom lies down with him about 40 minutes; he calls out to check she is awake; often ends up on parents' floor
Feared outcome at bedtime: someone breaking in while everyone sleeps and he can't get to mom
Dad leaves hall light on and door open
Soccer: mom stays in the parking lot every practice; he walked off the field mid-drill on the 13th
Sitter night: he texted repeatedly; parents came home early
agreed: Mom lies down for five minutes on a timer, then leaves
Rafael may call out to check once; mom does not answer further checks beyond a short goodnight
If he comes to the parents' room, walk him back to his own bed calmly
Rafael records his thermometer number before mom leaves and on waking
Hall light, soccer and sitter left unchanged this week

must_not_appear: A Fear Level for the sitter night (none was said)
That the hall light will be turned off this week
That mom will leave the soccer parking lot this week
A diagnosis such as separation anxiety disorder
